abstract: With the continuous development of electric vehicles and renewable energy, the rapid and accurate estimation of the State of Charge (SOC) of lithium batteries is crucial for energy storage applications. Traditional Open Circuit Voltage (OCV) measurements, which require prolonged battery rest, are not applicable during battery operation. Therefore, Ampere-Hour Integration is commonly adopted to estimate the battery SOC in real-time during charging and discharging processes. However, this method is prone to cumulative errors, making it challenging to accurately estimate SOC during prolonged battery operation. To address this issue, an adaptive SOC estimation method based on online OCV calibration is proposed in this paper. By establishing the equivalent circuit model (ECM) and combining the experimental test data, the functional relationship between the calibration voltage and the battery resting time is obtained to compensate for the terminal voltage measurement error caused by the battery polarization reaction. Then by using the calibrated OCV, combined with the OCV-SOC relationship obtained from the experimental test, the difference fitting method is used to realize the OCV-SOC online calibration. Based on the SOC estimation results after online OCV calibration, the K-value adaptive mathematical model is established to correct the accumulated error during Ampere-hour integration. Experimental validation and simulation analysis demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in compensating for OCV measurement errors caused by battery polarization and reducing cumulative errors in Ampere-hour integration.

articleTitle: Event-triggered grid-forming control for power converters via switching approach
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: This paper studies event-triggered grid-forming control for power converters via switching approach. Recently, grid-forming control based on matching of synchronous machines was suggested by using continuous measurements. In the present paper, we extend these results to the case where the measurements are sent to the controller via communication network. To reduce the network workload, we suggest an event-trigger (ET) via switching approach. Then the closed-loop system is presented as a switching between the system under periodic sampling and the one under continuous ET, where we take the maximum sampling preserving the stability as the lower bound of inter-event time avoiding the Zeno behavior. We construct appropriate Lyapunov functionals to derive linear matrix inequalities (LMIs) for finding the maximum sampling that guarantees the global exponential stability of a shifted equilibrium. Numerical case study illustrates the efficiency of the method.

articleTitle: Low-carbon Economic Dispatching Strategy of Park Integrated Energy System Considering Source Load Uncertainty
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Environmental problems and "double carbon" goals promote the development of the Carbon emission trading market and the construction of a park integrated energy system (PIES) with multiple energy complementarities. However, the uncertainties at both ends of the source and load bring certain challenges to the reliable operation of the system. This paper establishes a two-stage robust optimal scheduling model for the PIES, considering the impact of wind and solar load uncertainty on the scheduling strategy. In the first stage, the minimum cost of power purchase and hydrogen storage system operation is set as the objective function. In the second stage, the minimum cost of gas purchase, battery operation and Carbon emission trading is set as the objective function, and C&CG algorithm is adopted to solve the problem. Finally, the optimization and scheduling results of the comprehensive energy system in the park under different operating scenarios are verified.

articleTitle: Research on the Characteristics of Suppressing Photovoltaic Radiation Fluctuations in Ice Storage Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: This work built a photovoltaic driven steam compression refrigeration cold storage system (volume: 24.47m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>) was constructed, which adopts ice storage and energy storage technology to suppress photovoltaic fluctuations and ensure continuous and stable operation in off grid areas. Research has found that achieving sustained and stable energy supply under the coupling effect of photovoltaic fluctuations and ice storage/cooling was the key to efficient utilization of off grid photovoltaic cold storage systems. Analyzed the suppression characteristics of ice storage under different photovoltaic fluctuation times, and compared the non suppression and suppression. The results indicate that: When the photovoltaic fluctuation time < 7h, the stored cooling energy storage (Q<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ice</inf>) for suppressing fluctuations during the day was sufficient to support the cooling capacity released (Q<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rel</inf>) required for nighttime operation. When the photovoltaic fluctuation time > 6h, the stored Q<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ice</inf> for suppressing fluctuations during the day was insufficient to support the Q<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rel</inf> required for nighttime operation. Compared with non suppressed photovoltaic fluctuations, the refrigeration COP (COP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ref</inf>) and the system COP (COP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">sys,PV</inf>) increasing by 43.51% and 37.61% year-on-year, respectively. At the same time, suppress photovoltaic fluctuations and maintain the temperature in the warehouse at around 5 °C for all time periods after system operation. During the continuous operation of the photovoltaic cold storage system for 14 days, the total Q<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ice</inf> for 336h is 552.39 MJ, while the Q<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rel</inf> for the night and cloudy days is 442.23 MJ based on the needs of the cold storage system, and the remaining Q<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ice</inf> is 110.16 MJ.

articleTitle: Application of controllable resistive-type fault current limiter to low-voltage ride-through of DFIG
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: The resistive-type fault current limiter (FCL) may be applied to assist the low-voltage ride-through (LVRT) of the doubly-fed induction generator (DFIG). Considering the various fault scenarios, FCL with the fixed resistance may not provide flexible response to the different depths of terminal voltage drop. The controllable resistive-type fault current limiter (CRTFCL) is capable to adjust its resistance value to guarantee the satisfactory LVRT effect under different voltage drop depths. In this paper, the CRTFCL is applied to the LVRT of the DFIG. The different control targets of the DFIG during the LVRT, i.e., stator voltage control and active power output control, are selected and realized through the control to the resistance of the CRTFCL. The impact of the parameter setting of the CRTFCL resistance control on the LVRT effect is investigated. The numerical analysis is carried out with the different levels of the voltage drop. The control scheme to the CRTFCL resistance is simulated to show its feasibility and effectiveness to improve the LVRT effect of the DFIG.

articleTitle: Physics Informed Bellman Neural Network for Energy Management Strategy of Hybrid Electric Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Due to lower carbon emission and free of range anxiety, hybrid electric vehicles (HEV) have been more and more popular. In HEV, energy management system (EMS) plays an vital role in managing the usage of fuel and electricity. Dynamic programming (DP) is one of the most well-known methods, which can obtain the optimal solution. However, the ‘curse of dimensionality‘ makes it difficult and challenging to implement in most situations. In this paper, we use physics informed bellman neural network (PIBNN) to solve the optimization problem of the HEV. PIBNN has the ability to obtain the solutions of the Hamilton–Jacobi–Bellman (HJB) partial differential equation with required accuracy. Then, the state and control of the optimization problem of the HEV can be derived by conducting the interference step. Simulation results show the effectiveness and feasibility of the proposed methods.

articleTitle: Modeling and forecasting implied long term oil price with ARIMA model
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: The oil and gas play an important role in the global energy market and are considered one of the most fundamental traded products in the world. Oil and gas companies continuously seek to expand their asset portfolios and secure future energy supplies through strategic merger and acquisition (M&A). Considering the fact that the breakeven oil price is crucial for the operation performance and can impact the M&A decisions, this paper estimates the implied long term oil price (ILTOP) in the process of M&A for oil and gas companies. Based on the monthly data during March 2005-May 2023, this paper presented the trends of ILTOP and forecasted the short-term future price of ILTOP using the Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA) model. The results show that ARIMA(3,1,4) is appropriate for ILTOP within the specific time horizon. In addition, future ILTOP is estimated between 57~59 $/bbl in the following months. These findings can provide references for oil and gas companies to make investment and management decisions.

articleTitle: The combined application of vibration analysis and acoustic imaging for transformer fault detection
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Transformer is one of the most important equipment in power system, the fault detection of transformer has always been a topic that we need to study. The vibration analysis method and the Voiceprint detection method are very effective methods in the transformer live detection method. In this paper, the vibration signal and the sound pattern signal are collected by piezoelectric vibration sensor and array microphone respectively. According to the frequency concentration and vibration stationarity index that can be extracted from the vibration signal, a set of sound pattern vibration detection system is established, and the practical application of a 550kv transformer is carried out. According to the analysis of the detected data, it is concluded that there may be abnormal fastening fault in the A phase of the high voltage side of the transformer, which is consistent with the actual situation, and proves the effectiveness of the method.

articleTitle: Modified APC Strategy for Doubly Salient Electro-Magnetic Generator With Controlled Rectifier Considering Dramatic Load Changes
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: The output voltage of the traditional diode-rectified doubly salient electro-magnetic generator (DSEG) system will change significantly when the load current changes rapidly. Besides, it’s difficult to regulate the output voltage by adjusting the field current because of the large time constant. In order to solve the problem, a modified angular position control (APC) strategy based on the controllable rectifier DSEG system is proposed. Using the back propagation neural network (BPNN) to predict proper switching angles according to the speed and field current, the improved APC strategy is helpful to slow down the charge and discharge process of the capacitor and greatly reduced the output voltage fluctuation. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed strategy is proved by simulations on a 6/4 pole DSEG with controlled rectifier.

articleTitle: Research on Bidding Strategy of Virtual Power Plant Considering Dynamic Time-varying Domain
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: In the ancillary service market, different ancillary service products have different requirements for the time domain response behavior of bidding resources. Therefore, when virtual power plants(VPPs) aggregate management of controllable loads with many orders and significant difference in response characteristic, In addition to considering the power characteristics of controllable loads, they also need to consider the correspondence between the time domain response performance of controllable loads and different ancillary service demand. Firstly, the definition of time-varying feasible set of virtual power plant is clarified, and the dynamic partition construction method of virtual power plant is proposed to quantitatively analyze the fit of virtual power plant to different auxiliary services; Then, taking the virtual unit formed by aggregation as the minimum unit, an auxiliary service optimization bidding strategy considering the performance difference of bidding resources is constructed. Finally, a numerical example proves that the index ranking classification method can form a better bidding strategy, and verifies the feasibility and rationality of the virtual power plant optimization bidding strategy considering the difference in response performance of controllable loads.

articleTitle: Experimental Research on the Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cell Waste Heat Recovery System
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: The proton exchange membrane fuel cell combined heat and power (PEMFC-CHP) system can exploit the thermal energy and the electrical energy simultaneously, and the comprehensive utilization of energy efficiency is improved. The PEMFC-CHP system is considered as a promising low-carbon technology. Due to the strict requirements on the use and storage of the hydrogen, most of the current research on the PEMFC-CHP system is based on the simulation, and the experimental validation of the research on the waste heat recovery in the PEMFC-CHP system is limited. Therefore, a simulation experiment platform of the PEMFC waste heat recovery system is proposed in this paper. The PEMFC output characteristics and the thermal management methodology are analyzed. A control strategy of the PEMFC waste heat recovery system is proposed. Finally, the effectiveness of the control strategy is validated on the simulation experiment platform built.

articleTitle: Preparation and performance study of composite ceramic membrane heat exchanger tube based on membrane distillation process
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: In this paper, the application of hydrophobic ceramic membrane heat exchanger tubes based on membrane distillation technology in the field of waste heat recovery is studied. By hydrophobic modification of ceramic membrane tubes and designing a matching membrane heat exchanger, the heat transfer performance was analyzed. The optimal combination of hydrophobic modification experiments was determined, and a mathematical model was established for theoretical analysis and performance evaluation. Through experimental testing of the performance of membrane heat exchanger under different working conditions, it is concluded that the low flow rate and large temperature difference are not conducive to the progress of heat exchange and will aggravate the polarization phenomenon of temperature difference, while the more suitable experimental working condition combination is that the inlet flow rate of the liquid side of the pure water working fluid is 3.5L/min, the temperature difference between the cold and hot material liquid on both sides of the membrane is maintained at about 55 °C, the heat transfer coefficient value of the membrane heat exchanger can reach 1050W/(m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>∙ h), and the latent heat contribution rate can reach more than 40%. When the working medium of the hot material liquid is NaCl solution, its concentration is not higher than 3%, and the concentration effect can be ignored. The results of this study prove that membrane heat exchangers have important application value in the field of waste heat recovery, and provide experimental data and theoretical basis for research in this field.

articleTitle: A Right-and-Responsibility-Matching Network Usage Charge Scheme for Distributed Energy Trading
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Developing distributed renewable energy is vital to achieving the "carbon peak and carbon neutrality" goal. A suitable trading mechanism will prompt the generation and consumption of distributed renewable energy. The network usage charge is the core part of the market trading mechanism design. However, the current network usage charge scheme in China cannot recover the investment of power transmission and distribution assets, nor can it match the right and responsibility of distributed energy users. This paper proposes a method to calculate network usage charges, aiming at rationally recovering the investment costs of transmission and distribution assets of grid companies based on matching right and responsibility.

articleTitle: Calculation of the Maximum Hosting Capacity of Distributed Photovoltaics in Distribution Networks Considering Flexible Interconnections
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Large-scale access to distributed photovoltaics leads to power imbalance and frequent voltage fluctuations in distribution station areas, increasing the difficulty of operation control of distribution networks. To solve these challenges while improving the utilization rate of distributed photovoltaics, this study proposes a method for calculating the maximum hosting capacity (HC) of distributed photovoltaics in distribution networks, considering the flexible interconnection of low-voltage distribution station areas. First, two types of networking modes of the flexible interconnection of distribution station areas are analyzed and mathematical models are developed for them. Then, an optimization model of the maximum HC of distributed photovoltaics in a distribution network that considers the flexible interconnection of distribution station areas is established, and the increasingly tight linear-cut algorithm is used to solve it, which aims to narrow the gap introduced by the convex relaxation to get the optimal solution. Finally, the accuracy of the model and algorithm is checked in the modified IEEE 33-node distribution network.

articleTitle: Development of digital simulation system for switchgear operation status
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: This paper introduces the hardware and software components of the digital simulation system for switchgear operation status , and elaborates on the design concept, selection composition, operation mode and operation principle of the device. The device can simulate the operating status of intelligent electronic devices (IEDs) under various conditions accurately and reliably by comparing the simulation results retrieved from the network message analyzer with the actual typical waveforms through example simulation, which is of great practicality in the testing and acceptance of intelligent substation switchgear and helps to improve the intelligence level of substation equipment testing and maintenance.

articleTitle: Building Load Prediction Model Based on Integration of Mechanism and Data in District Heating Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: For the building load prediction in district heating systems, the traditional methods cover the mechanism models and the data-driven model. However, the data of the district heating systems was often of low quality or partly missing, and thus the traditional models cannot present high accuracy in load prediction due to the insufficient data available for training. This paper proposed a building load prediction model based on the integration of mechanism and data in district heating systems. The proposed model considered the heat transfer mechanism process and was trained by historical data. As for the training results in the scenario of insufficient data, the proposed prediction model presented a remarkable improvement by decreasing the MAPE and RMSE to 7.34% and 7.74%, respectively, on the same test dataset, compared with the data-driven model. The mechanism process integrated into the proposed model served as an additional feature and enhanced the data quality.

articleTitle: Optimal Power Flow for AC Power System based on Convex Relaxtion with Semi-Definite Programming
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: In this paper, the classical AC-OPF model is firstly introduced, and then it is relaxed into semi-definite (SD) OPF and second-order cone (SOC) OPF by the convex relaxation technique. Linear, SOC and SD OPF are compared in the example analysis. The high accuracy of SD OPF is verified. Compared with the classical AC OPF, the SD OPF model does not have the rank-one constraint, so the optimal solution may be outside the feasible area of the original OPF problem which is nonlinear and non-convex. This paper introduces two methods to obtain the exact solution, namely the penalty function method and the iterative algorithm based on convex-concave procedure principle, and then applies these two approaches to the case30 test system in the following part, where the feasibility of the two methods is verified.

articleTitle: Optimal Dispatch Strategy of Electric Vehicles under Coupled Transportation Network and Power Grid
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: This paper addresses the complex nature of electric vehicles (EVs) as both transportation means and mobile loads, and proposes an optimal dispatching scheduling strategy for EVs in the coupled transportation network and power grid. Firstly, a dynamic traffic network model is established by utilizing a vast amount of real-world traffic data, including Origin-Destination (OD) information, battery states, and departure times. A graph theory-based analysis is then employed to determine the optimal paths for EVs in the traffic network. Secondly, the charging behavior of EVs is integrated with the power grid, and charge-discharge scheduling is conducted for charging stations to optimize the power grid load curve while meeting the charging demands of EVs. Additionally, adaptive electricity prices are formulated based on the power grid’s load generation through a dynamic pricing mechanism, further optimizing the charging strategy for EVs. Lastly, the impact of EV charging on the power grid load is analyzed by contrasting ordered and unordered charging and discharging modes. The research results demonstrate that the proposed optimal charging scheduling strategy for EVs in traffic-aware power grids can significantly reduce peak-valley differences in power grid load, enhance the economic and operational stability of the power grid, and effectively meet the charging demands of EV users. These findings provide valuable insights and promising potential for practical applications and widespread adoption.

Author Keywords: Coupled Transportation Network and Power Grid

articleTitle: Research on Multi-application Strategy for Hybrid Energy Storage Considering Battery Life
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Due to the high impact and volatility of traction loads, the existence of large peak and valley differences, frequent and low utilization of the regenerative braking process, and the high coupling of planning and scheduling, it is difficult to plan the capacity configuration of the energy storage system (ESS). At the same time, the excessive charging and discharging of the battery will cause the loss of battery life, which also affects the economic efficiency of the traction power supply system (TPSS). In order to solve the above problems, this paper proposes a multi-application strategy that considers the lifetime of hybrid energy storage system (HESS). First, the characteristics of the HESS are analyzed when traction load shaving and regenerative braking energy (RBE) recovery are involved. Then, parameters are introduced to categorize the state of charge (SOC) intervals and energy management principles are developed. Finally, a two-layer optimization model with multi-application requirements is developed to solve the highly coupled problem of planning and scheduling of HESS. The improvement of the method on the planning-operating economy and battery life of the TPSS is verified by case analysis.

articleTitle: Coordinated Control Method of Power Oscillation Suppression for Multi-Parallel Synchronous Generator with Distributed Photovoltaic-Storage System
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: In order to effectively suppress the negative impact of the randomness and indirectness of photovoltaic output on the power grid, and improve the friendliness of the grid-connected photovoltaic-energy storage system, the coordinate control strategy of the distributed photovoltaic- energy storage system in the grid-connected mode has been investigated in depth. A power oscillation suppression method for multi-parallel synchronous inverters based on Virtual Synchronous Generator (VSG) to realize constant power control of Power Conversion System (PCS) and static-difference-free tracking of DC bus. The simulation research is carried out through the Matlab/Simulink platform, and the effectiveness of the control strategy is verified.

articleTitle: Optimization Strategy for Doubly Fed Induction Generator with Variable Coefficient Frequency Regulation
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: To solve the problem that Doubly Fed Induction Generator (DFIG) participate in power system frequency regulation through additional virtual inertia and droop control, but the fixed power control coefficients cannot bring into play the actual frequency regulation potential of the wind turbine, a frequency regulation strategy of variable coefficient control through quadratic function rectification formula is proposed. First, in order to improve the power support capability at frequency regulation, the over-speed and droop control is analyzed; then the quadratic function is rectified by the frequency deviation value to realize the variable coefficient weighting of the frequency regulation coefficient to realize the variable coefficient frequency regulation control; finally, the simulation model is built in MATLAB/Simulink simulation platform, and the results show that the proposed strategy can effectively improve the frequency regulation capability of the wind turbine.

articleTitle: Reliability Assessment of Active Distribution Network with Unclear Topology
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: In order to evaluate the reliability of distribution network with unclear topology, firstly, the reliability indices of three typical connection modes are calculated, and the reliability assessment model for distribution network with unclear topology is constructed. Then, considering the output characteristics and islanding operation of the distributed generation, typical connection modes are modified with the distributed generation access probability, and the influence of the distributed generation on the reliability is taken into account. Finally, the distribution network of Huizhou Huidong in 2019 is selected for analysis. The error of this method is 9%, and the distributed generation has little influence on the average interruption duration of regional distribution network. The results show that this method accurately reflects the reliability of distribution network with unclear topology, and fully considers the influence of distributed generation.

articleTitle: Research on the Debugging Strategy of Doubly Fed Variable Speed Pumped Storage Units
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Developing a scientific startup and debugging plan is a difficult problem that needs to be solved. Starting and debugging the generator can grasp the operating characteristics of the variable speed pumped storage generator and ensure its normal operation. Based on the basic principle analysis of variable speed pumped storage units, debugging strategy for doubly fed variable speed pumped storage unit is proposed in this paper. Analyze the roles and risks of each debugging project, and provide a safe and reliable debugging process for energy storage units. The strategy presented in this article was applied to debug a variable speed pumped storage power station in the southern power grid region. The shortcomings of the equipment were identified and corresponding solutions were provided, ensuring the normal operation of the pumped storage power station. It can provide reference for subsequent variable speed unit debugging and has important engineering value.

articleTitle: Grid-Connection Performance Evaluation of Renewable Energy Station
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: In the context of building a new-type power system with renewable energy as the main body, the grid connection performance evaluation index system and framework of renewable energy stations are put forward in order to accurately grasp the performance of renewable energy stations. Specifically, the calculation method of index including key electrical parameters, as well as the implementation method and platform are also given. Based on the analysis of simulation data and field tests, the grid connection performance evaluation index system of renewable energy stations constructed in this paper has certain advantages in data information accuracy and computational efficiency, which can provide a solution for the power grid to strengthen the perception and regulation ability of the grid connection characteristics for renewable energy stations.

articleTitle: Flexibility Upgrading of High Pressure Industrial Heating System for a Cogeneration Unit and its Performance Improvement
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: The governmental authority has set out ambitious objectives for enhancing peak load regulating capacity of existing fossil-fired generation units. Flexibility upgrading of co-generation units is one of the most challenging undertakings confronting the power industry. The peak shaving challenges of one co-generation unit with high-pressure industrial steam system have been addressed. A particular configuration of the high pressure industrial heating steam from the hot reheat steam source is introduced, which will induce high degree of coupling between heating and power generation and severely hamper the unit peak load regulating capacity. A novel flexibility upgrading scheme is proposed, which adopts the turbine main steam as the high pressure industrial heating steam source, and particulars including the advantages and disadvantages of the system are delineated. The model-based software suite EBSILON is employed for performance simulation of the exemplar 350MW supercritical co-generation unit under various industrial steam flow conditions, and detailed comparison is provided for the performance improvement achieved utilizing the proposed upgrading scheme. Results indicate that under HP turbine exhaust temperature limit of 338°C, with the proposed upgrading scheme, heating supply and power generation can be decoupled under various industrial steam flow conditions, mitigating minimum power output by around 50MW. Further analysis also demonstrates how the efficiency of HP and IP turbines varies with unit power output under the two schemes. Results also signify the existence of a cross point in the heat rate curves of the two schemes. Below the power output of this cross point, the proposed upgrading strategy accomplishes superior heat rate performance. The corresponding cross point power output are 300MW, 280MW and 240MW when high pressure industrial steam flow rates are 50t/h, 80t/h and 100t/h respectively.

articleTitle: Early warning of low-frequency oscillations in power system with Vinnicombe criterion fused with PMU data
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: With the development of the electricity industry in China, warning of low-frequency oscillations has become an important topic in power system stability research. In this paper, we propose a low-frequency oscillation warning method based on the downscaled Vinnicombe distance of key feature data. The method first screens and reduces the dimensionality of the PMU signals collected from the power system, initial feature matrix, and multi-feature vector state detection matrix for low-frequency oscillation amplitude warning indicators generated by key feature data extraction. The transfer function distance is calculated by computing the Vinnicombe distance, which judges whether low-frequency oscillation occurs and effectively improves the identification accuracy. Finally, algorithmic simulation through the New England 10-machine 39-node system is compared with the LOF method.

articleTitle: Reliability Assessment of Honeycomb Distribution Network Based on Quasi-Sequential Monte Carlo Simulation Method
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: In the context of "carbon emission peak and carbon neutrality", distribution systems in the future will evolve towards a new type of distribution system with high power supply capacity, high integration capacity for renewable energy, and high power supply reliability. This will result in forming of a honeycomb distribution network based on flexible power distribution technology. This paper presents a reliability analysis of a honeycomb distribution network based on a state transition model. Considering the different characteristics of components, the power base stations and distributed power sources are sampled using non-sequential sampling, while the non-power components in the system are sampled sequentially. This study examines the reliability of power supply under different fault scenarios. The results demonstrate that the honeycomb distribution network exhibits excellent performance in terms of power supply reliability, providing valuable insights for the planning and operation of honeycomb distribution networks.

articleTitle: Energy Optimization of Microgrids Based on Electricity-Carbon-Green Certificate Synergy
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: To accelerate the green-oriented transition of power system, the paper establishes a bi-level optimal decision-making model of microgrid under the coaction of electricity market, carbon market and green certificate market. The lower level, formed of the electricity market clearing model, carbon quota trading model and green certificate trading model, provides locational marginal prices (LMPs), carbon quota price and green certificate price for the upper level. The upper model can optimize the transaction and operation of the microgrid accordingly. Finally, the simulation analysis of IEEE-14 bus system proves that the model can effectively increase the consumption of renewable energy (RE) while reducing carbon emissions.

articleTitle: Robustness Assessment of Wind Power Prediction Under Cyber Security Attacks and its Impacts on Power System Operations
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Wind power prediction accuracy is closely related to the quality of wind power data. However, most of traditional prediction methods do not consider the cybersecurity of raw data. So, it would be important to study the prediction accuracy under false data injection attack (one type of cybersecurity attacks) and its influence on the economy and security of power system. In this paper, very short-term forecasting approach of wind power generation is studied for choosing the optimal prediction model. Different scenarios of false data injection attack are then simulated upon wind power data. Wind power prediction accuracy after being affected by false data injection is observed. The robustness of wind power prediction model is evaluated. Finally, wind power prediction information is applied to day-ahead unit commitment to evaluate the impact of cybersecurity of wind power forecasting on power system economy and security.

articleTitle: A State-of-health Estimation Method for LiFePO4 Batteries based on Gaussian Process Regression using Partial Charging Curve
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: The assessment of battery health has long been a major concern in lithium-ion battery applications. Effective and efficient approaches for the estimation of state-of-health (SOH) are crucial to LiFePO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> batteries with poor consistency. In this paper, we propose an estimation method based on Gaussian process regression (GPR) algorithm using partial charging curve. The curve is within a voltage range of only 60 mV, which is determined by a pre-analysis of voltage cumulative distribution. Considering the grade from grey relation analysis and the complexity to obtain, three interpretable health indicators are extracted from the charging voltage sequence as inputs to the model with a combined kernel function. The model achieves a root mean square error of 0.88% and outperforms several benchmark models on the tested public dataset. Furthermore, experimental results using data from the established platform reveal the high accuracy and adaptability of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Feasibility Study of DC Offshore Wind Farms Using Multiphase Generator-Rectifier
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: To obtain a cost-effective connection of electric power from offshore wind farms, two direct current (DC) grid schemes based on multiphase generator-rectifiers are proposed as alternatives to the conventional high voltage direct current (HVDC) scheme, which are direct step-up scheme for medium-distance wind farms and centralized step-up scheme for long-distance wind farms. The technical analysis indicates that the direct step-up scheme is appropriate for wind farms up to 200 km offshore, whereas the centralized step-up scheme exceeds this value. Meanwhile, the generator insulation for the two schemes are increased to ±80 kV and ±50 kV, and a potential insulation alternative is provided to prevent considerable increases in insulation thickness. Furthermore, the levelized cost of energy (LCoE) concept is used to compare the economics of the proposed schemes with the conventional HVDC scheme, using examples of 160 MW and 500 MW offshore wind farms. The analysis results show that the LCoE of the direct step-up scheme and the centralized step-up scheme are reduced by up to 9.2% and 3.7%, respectively. Therefore, the two proposed DC grid schemes have application potential for offshore wind farms.

articleTitle: Transient characterization of doubly fed induction generator during LVRT
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: This paper analyzes the transient characteristics of the DFIG at the Point of Common Coupling (PCC) during fault ride-through and the influence of the phase-locked loop(PLL) on its transient characteristics, constructs a time-domain model of the doubly-fed turbine under different grid strengths, and carries out simulations to verify the model. This paper also analyzes the causes of transient overvoltage in voltage recovery of DFIG and the influence of reactive power output on the voltage characteristics of DFIG during voltage recovery.

articleTitle: Power System Flexibility Assessment Method for Matching Supply and Demand with Flexibility
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: In recent years, the proportion of renewable energy, mainly wind power and photovoltaic, in the power system has been increasing, alleviating the environmental crisis and the problem of poor energy utilization. However, at the same time, the power system is increasingly affected by uncertainty factors, bringing many negative effects to the power system safety and reliability, etc. The fundamental reason is the lack of flexibility of the power system. In this paper, we first analyze the uncertainty of new energy output on the demand side of power system flexibility and the impact of error in load forecasting, and reflect the demand for power system flexibility through net load curve inscription. Then, this paper proposes four power system flexibility evaluation indexes starting from the basic parameters of the power system power supply side generating units. In order to better evaluate the matching degree between available flexibility resources and flexibility demand in the system, this paper further proposes a flexibility supply and demand matching index that takes into account flexibility demand and supply. Finally, the flexibility evaluation indicators were calculated and analyzed using actual operational data from a region in China to verify the validity of the evaluation indicators.

articleTitle: Data-driven Strategy for Model Identification and Voltage Estimation in Low-voltage Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: With the increasing penetration of residential distributed photovoltaics in low-voltage distribution Networks (LVDNs), problems such as three-phase imbalance, overvoltage and reverse overload are becoming increasingly prominent. However, it is difficult to build an accurate electrical model of LVDNs, thereby hindering accurate voltage estimation at each node and failing to provide a basis for formulating economical and effective control measures. To address this issue, this paper proposes a data-driven strategy for model identification and voltage estimation in LVDNs. The least squares method is used to identify the coefficients of the linear model between node phase voltage square and injection power, based on data collected by smart meters, in the presence of unknown network topology structure and parameters, coexistence of single-phase and three-phase loads, incomplete phase information and lack of voltage reference point. Based on the identified model, accurate estimation of voltage at each node is achieved. The proposed strategy has been effectively validated in a real LVDN and possesses characteristics that make it easy to deploy and applicable to engineering. It has significant potential for application in model-free LVDNs.

articleTitle: Design and Evaluation of Demand Side Market Based on Balance Unit Mechanism of German Electricity Market
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Designing a scientific demand-side market mechanism and guiding demand-side resources to play a flexible and regulating role is of great significance to ensuring the safe and stable operation of the new power system. As a country with a high degree of marketization of electricity, Germany has accumulated sufficient experience in promoting energy transformation and ensuring the stability of power grid operation. This paper draws on the experience of Germany and designs two demand side market construction schemes based on the current situation of Chinese demand-side resource participation in the market. The demand-side market evaluation index system is established from four dimensions: improving market economic benefits, ensuring grid operation efficiency, promoting renewable energy consumption, and maintaining market fairness and development. And based on the feasibility evaluation results, the advantages and existing problems of each scheme are discussed and summarized, and relevant suggestions are put forward for the construction of Chinese demand-side market.

articleTitle: Current Harmonic Suppression Method Based on SVHC and Improved SOGI for Active Power Filters
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: The rapid advancement and widespread application of power electronic technology have led to an exacerbation of harmonic pollution in power grids, necessitating research into effective solutions for harmonic control in power systems. In order to suppress the harmonic current, importance of the parallel active power filter (APF) is described and the modified control method of APF is proposed in this paper. Firstly, to solve the issue of inadequate harmonic suppression resulting from the disturbance of multiple harmonics in grid voltage, the harmonic detection method with instantaneous reactive power theory-based approach of i<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf>-i<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">q</inf> is adopted and the improved second-order generalized integrator (SOGI) is further proposed to improve the phase-locked loop (PLL). Secondly, a space vector hysteresis control (SVHC) strategy that combines hysteresis and space vector control, is proposed for harmonic current tracking. As validated by the simulations, the SOGI is effective and moreover, the proposed SVHC strategy outperforms the traditional hysteresis control in terms of the harmonic suppression and switching losses.

articleTitle: Event-Triggered State Estimation for Distribution Systems with SCADA and Smart Meter Data
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Accurate and timely state estimation plays an essential role in distribution systems. However, online distribution system state estimation (DSSE) calls for high measurement redundancy and communication resources. This paper is concerned with the SE problem for distribution systems with asynchronous measurements and limited communication resources. To alleviate the communication burden with the expansion of smart meter installation, a special open-loop event-triggered mechanism is designed for reducing unnecessary data transmission. And an event-triggered SE framework is tailored for distribution systems with asynchronous measurements, allowing for obtaining reliable state information at any desirable time. In the proposed SE framework, a robust linear estimator is provided for distribution systems with synchronous SCADA and smart meter data, in order to avoid the computation burden caused by the nonlinear measurement functions. Moreover, an l<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>-regularized least square-based SE is proposed for distribution systems with only SCADA measurements, where previous state information is used to avoid the under-determined problem. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed event-triggered SE is demonstrated using a sample 33-node distribution system.

articleTitle: Feedforward Tracking Control of Main Steam Temperature with Disturbance Rejection
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: As a commonly used control system, main steam temperature control has the characteristics of large inertia and large lag, and the noise interference it receives can also have a significant impact on the system. Faced with controlled objects with large inertia and delay, traditional control methods based on feedback regulation are difficult to quickly adjust the system, and it is also difficult to identify and control disturbances in advance. At the same time, although using feedforward control based on inverse models can quickly regulate the system, the strong differential effect caused by its sensitivity to high-frequency noise can lead to a decrease in regulation quality, so a feedback channel needs to be designed to address the impact of noise. This article introduces the basic principles of feedforward control, feedforward tracking control, and active disturbance rejection control, and points out areas for improvement. On this basis, a feedforward tracking control algorithm for main steam temperature with disturbance suppression is proposed. Through simulation experiments, its characteristics were analyzed and its control effect, anti-interference ability, and robustness were verified.

articleTitle: Development of Multi-Parameter Intelligent Diagnosis System for High-Voltage Cables
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: In response to issues such as the limited scope of high-voltage cable inspection techniques, low integration levels, and large size, this article designs a comprehensive parameter detection software and hardware platform for high-voltage cable equipment based on System on Chip (SoC). A miniaturized and multifunctional all-in-one detection terminal has been developed. Based on the fusion analysis of multiple physical quantities such as sound, light, and electricity under the same operating conditions, it enhances diagnostic accuracy and reduces diagnosis time. The effectiveness of the device was validated through on-site applications, achieving timely and accurate status monitoring and fault diagnosis of high-voltage cables.

articleTitle: Novel Overcurrent Protection Method for VSC-LCC Parallel Hybrid DC Transmission System
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: VSC-LCC parallel hybrid DC transmission system shares the same AC bus. When DC line of VSC or LCC system fails, in addition to the protection operation configured in this protection zone, it will also cause current fluctuation in AC connection line area of VSC system, resulting in over-current protection malfunction. To address this issue, a new overcurrent protection judgment method was proposed by analyzing typical characteristic waveforms of VSC-LCC parallel hybrid system under different regional faults in this paper. This method utilizes the voltage change rate of the DC line in VSC system and the grid-side voltage fault component of the connecting transformer as criteria to solve the problem of overcurrent protection malfunction in the AC connection line area of the VSC system caused by DC line faults. It is of great significance for rapid fault isolation and improving the safe and stable operation ability of parallel hybrid DC system.

articleTitle: Doubly Grounded Dual-Input Transformer-less Three-phase Inverter for PV-battery system
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Traditional three-phase photovoltaic (PV) inverters have common mode leakage current and are highly susceptible to the influence of light intensity. In order to solve this problem, three-phase double-grounded PV inverter with integrated battery energy storage is proposed in this paper. The system consists of PV modules, energy storage units and three-phase bridge inverter. In order to maximize the use of solar energy, the perturbation observation method is used to realize the maximum power point tracking (MPPT) of PV modules, and the corresponding charging control strategy is proposed for the energy storage units based on the state of charge balance of the battery pack, which realizes the power flow of the system and meets the normal operation of the PV inverter under different lighting conditions. The feasibility of the proposed inverter and control strategy is verified through simulation.

articleTitle: Organic Rankine cycle and absorption heat pump energy system based on valley electricity utilization and molten salt energy storage
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: In order to effectively utilize valley electricity and reduce energy consumption, a nighttime valley electricity energy storage system based on molten salt was developed. Reduced daytime energy costs are achieved by utilizing the Organic Rankine Cycle and air source absorption heat pumps to release during the day. Through energy analysis, exergy analysis and economic analysis, the performance of the system is evaluated. The results show that the total energy efficiency of the system can reach 50.37%, which is at a relatively high level. Steam turbine and HST are the two equipment with the largest energy loss. The exergy analysis shows that the exergy output of the system is not much different from the heat supply. A simple economic analysis evaluates the difference between using molten salt energy storage during the day and not using molten salt energy storage. The results show that the cost of electricity and heating with energy storage in the valley is only half of that without energy storage.

articleTitle: Research on adjustable load classification and aggregation and external characteristic identification method
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: With the acceleration of the construction process of the new power systems, virtual power plants have developed rapidly. To enable a large number of adjustable loads to effectively participate in grid operation and market transactions, virtual power plants need to realize the aggregation of adjustable loads. Firstly, a load classification method based on comprehensive response performance indexes (CPRI) is proposed in this paper. Then, the adjustable loads are aggregated into virtual units according to the NJW (Ng, Jordan, Weiss) spectral clustering algorithm, and the external characteristics of the virtual units are defined. Finally, the feasibility of the proposed method is verified by analysis of example.

articleTitle: Research on the Influence of 500 kV Fault Current Limiter on Line Distance Protection
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Fault current limiters(FCLs) are effective measures to limit short-circuit current(SCC). However, traditional FCLs have a relatively long operating time. This article proposes an economical fault current limiting device with a large capacity and fast switch in parallel with a high impedance current limiting reactor. It takes 6 to 20 ms from fault occurrence to reactor operation, and the duration is far less than 60 to 100 ms needed for general relaying and circuit breaker on-off at least; At the same time, the operational features of the new FCL were analyzed, and the mechanism of the change in line parameters caused by the connection of the FCL, which in turn affects distance protection, was studied. Finally, a simulation analysis was conducted on a real power grid to demonstrate the validity of the proposed measure.

articleTitle: Numerical study on the influence of Helmholtz resonators on gas mixing performance
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Helmholtz Resonators are extensively used in various engineering applications to control acoustic phenomena, but their impact on gas mixing has not been studied yet. In this research, numerical flow simulations within a channel in the presence of Helmholtz resonators were conducted to model the gas mixing process inside the channel and investigate the effect of increasing the number of resonators on the mixing process. The Fluent 2022R2 was utilized for solving the unsteady Reynolds-averaged Navier-Stokes equations. The fluid was considered compressible, and the K‒ε turbulence model was used to model turbulence. To validate the numerical results, a test rig was prepared to measure the frequency and pressure oscillation amplitude inside the resonator, and the numerical results were compared with the experimental results. The numerical results revealed the significant role of Helmholtz resonators in enhancing gas mixing. Vortex shedding at the cavity edge and generating positive and negative pressure waves in opposite cavities led to oscillatory flow in the channel and the mixing of two gases. Increasing the resonators to three pairs resulted in even greater gas mixing enhancement so that the difference between the maximum and minimum temperatures of the two gases at the outlet decreased by 87% compared to that at the inlet. These findings provide deeper insights into the underlying mechanisms on gas mixing and offer insights for designing and optimizing mixing systems in various industrial processes.

articleTitle: A Fault Diagnosis Model for Wind Turbine Blade Using a Deep Learning Method
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: A wind turbine plays a pivot role in the field of energy supply. A stable working state of the wind turbine is highlighted in power generation. For this reason, it is thus of great interest to develop a fault diagnosis method for status identification of wind turbine. In this work, the imbalance of turbine blade is investigated on the task of fault diagnosis. Vibration sensors are attached to the blade to detect vibration signals. A deep learning based method using gated convolution neural network and long short term memory unit, together with the attention mechanism, is established. The application of the proposed model is capable of capturing the most-related features that characterize the working states. The working performance of the proposed model is validated on the samples from various working conditions. The experimental results set solid evidence of a high accuracy.

articleTitle: A File Transfer Method Based on Modbus Protocol
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Aiming at the demand for file transfer via fieldbus in power system terminal equipment and the lack of application cases of common file transfer protocols in fieldbus, this paper proposes a file transfer method based on Modbus protocol. The method is based on Modbus basic function code, and uses the TFTP-like protocol embedded in Modbus data frames for file transfer. The specific format of the transfer frames is proposed, the frame interaction process of file transfer is described, and the error control mechanism and failure exit mechanism during the transfer process are analyzed. The Modbus protocol-based file transfer is implemented. The experimental results show that the method can achieve reliable file transfer between master and slave devices. Compared with other file transfer methods, the method is simple, highly portable, and suitable for Modbus communication networks with low requirements for file transfer speed.

articleTitle: A brain-inspired spiking neural network for the renewable energy short circuit ratio prediction
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: With the skyrocket of renewable energy integration, the scale of long-distance power transmission and consumption has gradually expanded. The voltage support strength of the generation system is easily affected by the unexpected fluctuation of the onsite renewable energy stations, which seriously affects the power system stability. Previously, the short-circuit ratio (SCR) is widely utilized for grid strength detection, as it can reflect the situation clearly and intuitively. Therefore, the renewable energy short-circuit ratio (RESCR) is constructed to keep the step with the power system transformation. The RESCR is a crucial indicator for power shifting and protection scheme design. However, due to the undesired fluctuation of renewable power, the RESCR deviates more severely than the conventional SCR index. Thus, the RESCR prediction research is significant for regulating and operating the power generation system. The RESCR prediction methods mostly use traditional artificial neural networks with large power consumption. To solve this problem, we proposed a prediction model based on residual structure and spiking neural networks called SpikeNet, which has the characteristics of event-driven and sparse representation and can realize low-power computing. Based on this model, we also proposed a novel training framework that includes a pre-training process and an online prediction process. In the pre-training process, the network can learn basic prediction knowledge based on historical data. The network can obtain continual learning capability through secondary learning in the online prediction process. Based on the utility-side historical data, we construct a dataset used for pre-training and then verify the proposed prediction model's online function.

articleTitle: Power System Restoration Method With the Flywheel Energy Storage Support
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Since energy storage has the characteristic of adjustable charging/discharging, its application to power system restoration can efficiently assist in shortening the outage time. Based on this, this paper proposes a power system restoration method considering flywheel energy storage. Firstly, the advantages and disadvantages of various types of energy storage are analyzed by comparison. Flywheel energy storage is selected for power system restoration. Secondly, a restoration model for power systems considering flywheel energy storage is constructed. The objective function is to maximize the amount of restored load. Except for conventional restoration constraints, the constraint on flywheel energy storage is proposed. Finally, the IEEE 39-bus test system is used as an example simulation to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A method for improving small-signal stability via optimal allocation on the virtual inertia
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: The shortage of inertia in renewable energy power systems can be resolved with virtual synchronous generators (VSG) control technology to furnish inertia support for the systems. In this paper, a virtual inertia optimal method is proposed to improve the small-signal stability of power systems. The objective of the proposed model is to maximize the minimum damping ratio of the system with constraints, such as the small-signal stability and the capacity for regulation. For solving the aforementioned model, the reduced note admittance matrix of the system is solved to obtain the state matrix of the simplified system, and the sensitivity analysis algorithm is adopted for the optimal allocation of virtual inertia. Through each iteration, the minimum damping ratio of the state matrix increases. Simulation results demonstrated the good performances of the proposed optimal method in improving the small-signal stability, and it has the potential for practical application in complex power grids.

articleTitle: Application Analysis of Intelligent Monitoring System in Pumped-storage Hydroelectricity
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Under the background of the development trend and demand of Pumped-storage hydroelectricity intelligence and digitalization, this paper first analyzes the sensor configuration demand and traditional application drawbacks of Pumped-storage hydroelectricity; Secondly, the application feasibility of intelligent sensor in Pumped-storage hydroelectricity is analyzed; Then, the differences in intelligent sensor types and communication protocols were compared and analyzed; Finally, the framework of panoramic monitoring and early warning system suitable for Pumped-storage hydroelectricity and relevant Functional requirement are proposed to provide the corresponding Technology roadmap for the actual intelligent construction of Pumped-storage hydroelectricity.

articleTitle: Capacity and Operation Planning Model of Energy Storage System in Power Spot Market
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: To promote the development of energy storage system (ESS) technology and the configuration of ESS in power system under the background of power market, this paper establishes a two-stage optimization model of capacity and operation planning based on the participation of ESS in power spot market. Firstly, the mechanism of ESS participating in the spot market is expounded and the market operation cost and benefit are modeled. Secondly, the first-stage capacity planning model is constructed with the goal of minimizing the initial investment, maintenance and operation costs of ESS and the total operation costs of conventional units, and the optimal ESS capacity can be obtained by solving the first stage model. Then, the second-stage optimal scheduling model is constructed with the goal of minimizing the electricity purchase costs of the market operator, and the revenue of ESS in the electric energy market and auxiliary service market is calculated. Finally, the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed method are verified by a modified IEEE-30 system case.

articleTitle: Two-stage charge and discharge optimization of battery energy storage systems in microgrids considering battery state of health
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: An important figure-of-merit for battery energy storage systems (BESSs) is their battery life, which is measured by the state of health (SOH). In this study, we propose a two-stage model to optimize the charging and discharging process of BESS in an industrial park microgrid (IPM). The first stage is used to optimize the charging and discharging time and the corresponding amount of the charging and discharging energy from the BESS, in which the SOH is considered. Subsequently, all battery packs need to be coordinated to ensure a reasonable BESS operation. In order to prolong the service life of the BESS, the second stage of the model allocates the charging and discharging of all battery packs on the basis of the first stage scheduling results. The proposed loss-calculation method is used to calculate the battery pack loss and then to calculate the SOHs of battery packs. It can be seen from the simulation results that the scheduling results considering the SOH are more realistic. Furthermore, the proposed charging and discharging allocation strategy can effectively coordinate the SOH change of all battery packs without causing a significant increase in the battery pack loss of the battery packs.

articleTitle: Analysis and research on generator design technology of variable speed pumping and storage units at home and abroad
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: With the establishment of the national "carbon peak" and "carbon neutral" goals, the state clearly proposed to increase the development of clean energy, including the development of variable speed pumping and storage units, at present, Germany, Japan and other countries have earlier development of variable speed pumping and storage units, technical capabilities, application performance are wider, there is a greater reference significance. This paper discusses several technical routes for the key generator design of variable speed pumping and storage units, and puts forward a concrete optimization scheme[1].

articleTitle: A Robust Parameter Identification Strategy of Composite Load Model With a Neural Differential Algebraic Network
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Recently, the ambient signal (AS) based load identification method has been favored by researchers due to its ability to capture the time-varying nature of load characteristics. However, load characteristics are not sufficiently perturbed by small disturbances, leading to the easy distortion of effective signals in AS, and inaccurate identification results that cannot reflect the actual load composition and model parameters. To address this issue, this paper proposes a real-time load composition estimator based on a neural differential-algebraic equations network (NDAE) to guide the parameter optimization process. Moreover, considering the redundancy of AS, a hierarchical strategy based on the verification and synthesis of multiple sets of identification results is designed to improve the reliability of the final conclusion. The effectiveness of the proposed strategy is verified using the WSCC 9-node simulation system.

Index Terms: Least Absolute Shrinkage And Selection Operator

articleTitle: Numerical Study on the Influence of Coal Ash Particle Concentration and Particle Size in Flue Gas on Heat Transfer of Fire Tube Waste Heat Boiler
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: In order to study the influence of ash particle concentration and particle size in flue gas on the heat transfer performance of waste heat boiler, the Euler-Lagrange method was used to simulate the gas-solid two-phase flow and heat transfer in the heat exchange tube of waste heat boiler. The results indicate that: in a certain concentration range, the average heat transfer coefficient of heat exchange tube wall increases with the increase of particle concentration. The deposition rate of coal ash particles on the wall of the heat exchange tube is approximately linearly related to the concentration of coal ash particles. When the concentration of coal ash particles is high, the larger the particle size, the greater the impact on heat transfer. Particle size 30 μm and 35 μm the coal ash particles are prone to deposition on the pipe wall. Particle size between 5-30 μm the sedimentation rate of particles within the range of will increase with the increase of particle size. The particle size of coal ash particles is 5 μm, the performance of the heat exchange tube is optimal. The radiation heat transfer caused by the increase in the concentration of coal ash particles is greater than the convective heat transfer caused by their disturbance to the flue gas. The influence of particles on heat transfer in the heat exchange tube is mainly due to the radiation effect of particles.

articleTitle: Diesel generator sensor fault diagnosis model based on LMD-SVM algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: For the fault diagnosis of a diesel generator sensor system, a fault diagnosis model of diesel generator sensor based on the coupling of LMD and SVM algorithm is proposed, firstly, the fault signal is collected and the fault features are extracted by using LMD demarcation, then it is combined with SVM model, and the SVM classifier parameters are optimized by using the modified particle swarm algorithm (MPSO) to further improve the accuracy of fault diagnosis. The experimental results show that the accuracy of fault diagnosis of diesel generator sensor system (vibration sensor, temperature sensor, voltage sensor, and current sensor) using LMD-SVM model can reach 96.9%, 95.3%, 95.8%, and 94.8%, which has better diagnosis effect.

articleTitle: Study on Thermal-physical Property of MWCNTs Nanofluids and Photo-thermal Conversion
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Solar thermal collectors are devices used to efficiently utilize solar energy. This study experimentally investigates the effects of multi-walled carbon nanotubes (MWCNTs) nanofluids on the efficiency of solar thermal collectors. The MWCNTs nanofluids are prepared by two-stage process. The thermal conductivities of both the basic fluids and MWCNTs nanofluids have been investigated using a thermal constant analyzer. Furthermore, the photo-thermal conversion performances of both the basic fluids and MWCNTs nanofluids are analyzed using a solarization experiment. The results indicate that the thermal conductivity of MWCNTs nanofluids increases with an increasing volume fraction and suspension stability of nanoparticles, while decreasing with an increasing dispersant concentration. For the same volume fraction, MWCNTs-EG nanofluids exhibit higher thermal conductivities and better suspension stability compared to MWCNTs-DW nanofluids. However, the efficiencies of solar thermal collectors that use MWCNTs-DW nanofluids as the working fluid are higher than those that use MWCNTs-EG nanofluids. The maximum efficiency for MWCNTs-DW nanofluids reached 55.59%, which is 12.98% higher than that of MWCNTs-EG nanofluids.

articleTitle: Optimal Planning for Energy Storage Plants Considering Location and Configuration
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: To determine the location and configuration for energy storage plants, this work establishes the optimization method of energy storage plants based on the energy balance and constraints. This is applicable for the location selection and capacity determination. Firstly, the location is pre-selected considering load, installed capacity of renewable energy, and average distance of neighboring nodes. The location and configuration of the plants are optimized through the multi-objective artificial bee colony algorithm with maximizing the peak-shaving profit, minimizing the investment cost and active network loss as evaluation indicators. The tide calculation is performed with the lowest operating cost as the objective, and the hourly optimal charging and discharging power are optimized. The results show that the proposed method can effectively realize the optimization of location and capacity for energy storage plants, and the renewable energy utilization can be promoted.

articleTitle: Economic Scheduling of Multi-microgrid Systems Based on Distributed Event-triggered Consensus Strategy
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Multi-microgrid (MMG) systems offer notable advantages in terms of power sharing and mutual support when compared to individual microgrids (MGs). This paper presents a based on distributed event-triggered consensus strategy for optimizing the economic dispatch of multiple microgrids. The incorporation of the event-triggered mechanism into the multi-microgrid framework significantly reduces unnecessary communication among microgrids in contrast to the conventional time-triggered approach. For the multi-microgrid setup, a two-layer control strategy consisting of inter-microgrid and intra-microgrid layers is employed to achieve coherence by regulating the micro-incremental rates of distributed generation (DG) units. Leaderless event-triggered consistency is utilized for inter-microgrid coordination, while leader event-triggered consistency is implemented for intra-microgrid coordination, ultimately realizing the economic objective of minimizing the operational costs of the multi-microgrid system. Simulation results validate the efficacy of introducing the event-triggered mechanism and its impact on the economic dispatch of the multi-microgrid system.

articleTitle: Protection Logic Based on Intelligent Phase Change Switch Phase-to-Phase Short Circuit Fault
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: With the rapid development of distributed photovoltaic industry and new energy electric vehicles as well as flexible DC transmission, the phenomenon of three-phase imbalance in the distribution station area is becoming more and more serious. The phase change switch can solve the problem of three-phase unbalance by regulating the load balance and has been applied in the power grid. However, the current topology of phase change switches is generally defective in terms of phase-to-phase short circuits, which is a threat to the normal operation of the grid if the equipment fails. In this paper, we analyze the topology of the phase change switch, derive the defects of the topology, and propose a phase short circuit protection logic to address the defects. The protection logic interlocks the trigger signals of the phase change switch manipulator to effectively avoid phase short circuit faults. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed protection logic is verified by MATLAB/Simulink simulation. The simulation results show that the phase-to-phase short-circuit protection logic avoids the risk of faults that may be caused by the phase change switch and makes its operation more stable and reliable.

articleTitle: Control Strategy of Voltage Compensation with Harmonics for Dynamic Voltage Restore
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: The widespread use of a large number of distributed power supplies such as photovoltaic, wind power and other equipment may bring power quality problems such as voltage fluctuations to the grid, and may cause damage to a large number of user side equipment, resulting in huge losses. Therefore, in order to ensure the stable operation of the system, how to restore the dynamic voltage to keep the stable voltage without fluctuation on the user side is particularly important. In this article, the dynamic voltage restorer is proposed to take the compensations for voltage fluctuation with harmonics accurately. The fast voltage fluctuation detection and high compensation depth Improved Synchronous Reference Frame (ISRF) method are proposed for handling the grid voltage with amplitude fluctuation and harmonics, to ensure that the user side voltage is not affected. In the aspect of harmonic extraction, the method of Butterworth high-pass filter is proposed.
